interest: This document offers a revealing glimpse into Japanese pre-World War II naval intelligence gathering and maritime reconnaissance along the Indian Ocean and East African coastlines. It highlights the use of civilian maritime covers—specifically deep-sea fishing operations—by Japanese naval officers to survey strategic foreign ports and approaches such as Mombasa. Additionally, the file's cross-references to German (862.20248t) and Italian (865.20248t) files illustrate U.S. diplomatic interest in monitoring potential Axis intelligence networks and military interests across colonial territories in Africa.
overview: This file consists of a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.20248 (and 894.20248T), concerning Japanese military activities, espionage, and information gathering in British East Africa (Kenya). The file indexes Despatch No. 42 from Consular Officer Smith in Nairobi to the State Department's Far Eastern and European divisions. The entry records a report detailing how a group of Japanese naval officers had operated out of Mombasa for roughly three years under the pretense of being deep-sea fishermen to conduct coastal reconnaissance, eventually returning to Japan at the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers docket sheet indexing a report on Japanese espionage activities in British East Africa.
subfiles.summary: This document is an index docket sheet listing records under State Department decimal file 894.20248 regarding Japanese military activities in British East Africa. It indexes Nairobi Despatch No. 42 sent by Smith to the Far Eastern and European divisions on March 7. The summarized despatch reports on Japanese naval officers posing as deep-sea fishermen in Mombasa to conduct coastal reconnaissance before returning home at the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities.
